paper.title_en: A minimal fractional deformation of Newtonian gravity: a unified description of cosmology and weak-field tests
paper.abstract_en: We investigate a minimal fractional deformation of Newtonian gravity as a unified effective framework for cosmology and weak-field gravitational tests. Here we demonstrate that a single-parameter fractional extension of the Newtonian action, motivated by fractal frameworks in field theory with a Stieltjes-type measure, gives rise to an effective framework capable of reproducing gravitational dynamics across vastly different scales. Previous studies of this framework have addressed cosmic evolution, including a nonsingular pre-inflationary phase, an inflationary attractor, radiation- and matter-dominated epochs, and the present accelerated expansion. The evolution of matter density perturbations has also been investigated, with results compatible with cosmological constraints. These applications share a unified effective potential description without introducing additional dynamical degrees of freedom. In this paper, we extend this construction to weak-field gravity, showing that key tests such as the perihelion precession of Mercury and the deflection of light grazing the solar limb are consistently described within the same potential, with all constraints pointing to only a small deviation from standard Newtonian dynamics. These results support a unified effective description of cosmological evolution and weak-field gravity, providing a basis for exploring the smallness of the effective cosmological constant, the hierarchy of Hubble scales, and the Hubble tension.
